column1: # SUBTLEX-US word frequencies — the 20,000 most frequent surface forms.
# Brysbaert, M., & New, B. (2009). Moving beyond Kučera and Francis: A critical
# evaluation of current word frequency norms and the introduction of a new and
# improved word frequency measure for American English. Behavior Research
# Corpus: 51 million words of American English film and television subtitles.
# Obtained through the ISC-licensed repackaging words/subtlex-word-frequencies
# keeps the Word and FREQcount columns of SUBTLEXus74286wordstextversion.txt.
# The authors permit redistribution of SUBTLEX-US for any purpose. This file is
# that list sorted by count, truncated to the first 20,000 rows, on 2026-09-12.
# Columns: rank, word, count. A word is capitalized when the corpus more often
# capitalizes it than not ("I", "Mr", "Congratulations"). Contraction fragments
# ("s", "t", "don") are present because the source splits on apostrophes.
# Surface forms, not lemmas. Generated — do not edit by hand.
